helps.text:
Syntax: multi <class>
        multi

Sentience allows a multiclassing system which allows you to multi
four times into a total of four different classes. Every time you
multi is like going back to level 1. You will learn new skills and
spells as well as old ones from previous classes by levelling up.

'multi' without an argument shows the classes you may multi to.

You may multi to the different classes in any order of your choosing.
Multiclassing occurs at level 30, 60, and 90. Your first multi at
level 30 is free, but for subsequent classes you must venture to the
Demon Plane to collect bottled souls and return them for Pneuma, a
measure of your essence. The second multi at level 60 costs 500
pneuma, and the level 90 multi costs 1000.

After these four classes, Sentience allows you to remort.
In order to do this, you must recover the four remort runes,
allowing your character to gain more power with new skills
and spells.

As a remort, multiclassing takes much more Pneuma.  Unlike before,
the first multi isn't free.  It costs 2500 to multi as a level 30
remort, 5000 as a level 60, and 10000 for the final multi as a remort.
 
To multiclass, you must be at a guildmaster.

Syntax: practice
		practice <skill>
		train
		train <stat>

PRACTICE shows you all of the skills you currently have.
To practice a skill, you must be at a trainer. Enclose skills
with more than one word in quotes (i.e. practice 'second attack').

TRAIN trains an attribute such as hp, mana, int, wis, etc. Train
without any arguments shows you all of the attributes you can train.

See also: convert

helps.text:
Syntax: quest request
		quest complete
		quest points
		quest list
		quest buy <item>
{x    quest sell <item>
{x    quest inspect <item>
		quest info
		quest time

Certain mobiles in the game known as questmasters
will give you a quest to benefit their kingdom. Completing
a quest successfully will yield quest points which can
in turn be used to buy a variety of special items from the
quest master. Upon completion an adventurer might also receive
money and practices, which is decided on a random basis.

QUEST REQUEST - Requests a quest from the questmaster.
QUEST COMPLETE - Completes the quest.
QUEST POINTS - Displays how many quest points you currently have.
QUEST LIST - Lists available quest items.
QUEST BUY - Buys an item from the questmaster.
QUEST INSPECT - Inspect an item for sale.
QUEST SELL - Sell a quest item to the questmaster.
QUEST RENEW - Update an item to be your current level for 1/10 its price.
QUEST INFO - Shows you information about your current quest.
QUEST TIME - Shows you how much time you have left until you
		can get another quest or how much time you have left
		on your current quest.

Syntax: save
		quit

Save writes your player file to disk, preserving character data.
It's not really necesarry to do this unless you are extremely paranoid,
as the game automatically saves character data every 15 minutes or so.

Quit leaves the game. A save is done automatically when you quit, so
saving before quitting is not necesarry.

Thieves all across the world have trained to better prevent themselves
from being struck in combat.  Simply dodging attacks was not enough for the
light armored, delicate bodies of the thieves.  They decided to add a little
more dexterity into their movements when avoiding attacks; backflipping over
low attacks, doing the splits under high attacks.  Their new acrobatic
styled defense became a staple for all thieves' defenses.  Any thief
proficient in the acrobatics skill can reduce the number of hits they take
in battle, and therefore, tend to live a little longer.

Archery is an automatic skill known to Elves and
rangers. Knowledge of archery lets a user target their
prey more quickly, and increases their firing accuracy
proportional to how well they know it.

helps.creator: Syn
helps.text:
Athletics is a Destroyer skill dedicated to saving one's
energy during combat. This skill is automatic and does not need
to be activated. It allows for faster regeneration of movement
as well as less movement expense in battles.

helps.creator: none
helps.text:
Syntax: backstab <target>

BACKSTAB is the preferred skill of rogues and thieves who prefer to use
their sly skills to doing combat. It belts an enemy in the back
with a dagger, causing severe damage. The damage caused depends on your
level, the victim's level, and your backstab skill. Since it requires
that one sneak up on a target, it cannot be used in the middle of combat.

helps.creator: none
helps.text:
Syntax: bash <target>
{x        bash <direction>
 
BASH is a powerful skill that knocks your opponent to
the ground with brutal force. Its success depends on the
level and size difference between you and your opponent.
It can also be used to open stubborn doors; however, some
doors are made of strong materials and thus impervious to.
bashing.

helps.creator: Ertai
helps.text:
{YBEHEAD{x
When a destroyer senses that its victim is nearing thier last breath,
they will look towards this gruesome way of delivering the final blow.
At a time deemed appropriate and effective, one might cleave an opponents
head off, sending it flying through the air.  Few have lived to witness
this grisly spectacle.
 
Credited to: Upir

helps.creator: Syn
helps.text:
This skill allows the Warlord to bind together serious wounds using
whatever supplies are at hand.  It is a skill which should only be invoked
in the direst of need, as the practitioner can't fight while tending to the
wounded. If used properly it will tide over the seriously injured until more
medical attention arrives.

helps.creator: none

Syntax: blackjack <victim>
 
The blackjack skill is an age-old favourite of the 
talented thief. It may only be used when the victim is sneaking.
A successful blackjack will bolt a victim in the back of the head
and render them unconscious for a period of time; however, it is difficult
to pull off successfully if the victim has high dexterity.
the "calm" spell makes a person immune to blackjack, as does
a helmet with the "super-strong" flag such as the Helm of Alemnos.

Syntax: circle
 
Circle is the acclaimed skill of a gladiator, 
in which they will circle around their opponent
and strike them blindsided, devestating them
with this brutal way of engagement, causing
massive injury.

Although generally considered cowardly, it is no less effective.

Syntax: disarm <person>
 
the DISARM skill attempts to rid an opponent of his weapon
by knocking it out of his hands. Those protected by the Death
Grip spell cannot be disarmed.
 
See also: death grip

helps.text:
The proficiency at the skill is your ability to dextrously dodge blows in combat. It
success depends on your dodge skill and your dexterity.

helps.creator: none
helps.text:
Fast healing is a warrior's ability to heal from their wounds
faster. It represents one's stamina and general health, and
can improve quickly as the player heals, depending on their
skill in it.

helps.creator: none
helps.text:
Syntax: flee
		flee <direction>

FLEE attempts to run away from combat in cowardice.
Without an argument, flee picks a random direction
to try an escape to, but you can also specify
a direction (i.e. 'flee north').

helps.creator: Azrael
helps.text:
Syntax: holdup <target>

Holdup is a skill used by the Highwaymen only.  In a space of a
heartbeat, a skilled highwayman can hold his weapon to a victim's throat,
incapacitating them for the duration of the holdup.  As soon as the
highwayman makes any action, whether to attack, steal, leave the room, or
even look around, the holdup ends.  If a highwayman fumbles and are clumsy
with their weapon, he leaves himself vulnerable to being attacked or
disarmed.

helps.creator: none
helps.text:
Syntax: intimidate <target>
 
Intimidate is a well known skill of the minotaur, in
which they will strike up a pose, giving an evil look
to the unsuspecting traveler, scaring them so bad that
they run away in fear of their life. The more knowledged
a minotaur is in this skill, the better chance one has
of intimidating a traveler so bad that they run away
horrified at the site of you.
 
see also: MINOTAUR

helps.creator: none
helps.text:
Syntax: kick <target>
 
KICK delivers a martial-arts style kick to an opponent's 
midsection, providing a devestating effect.

helps.creator: Elden
helps.text:
Martial arts is a skill that works automatically to improve your skill in
hand to hand combat.

helps.creator: Azrael
helps.text:
This special ability of the crusader gives him an uncanny ability to
steer a mount and fight at the same time.  Any weapon can be used, although
those with a bit more range are preferred.  The Crusader also gets the
assistance of his mount in battle, such as crushing, kicking, biting, and
all the other things a good warhorse is made for.

helps.creator: none
helps.text:
Parry blocks incoming attacks with your weapon.  All warriors have
knowledge of this skill. Its success depends on your parry skill, your
dexterity and the opponent's dexterity, your skill at your weapon, your
opponent's skill at his weapon, and the relative weight of both your weapons
(e.g.  It's difficult to block a heavy weapon with a light one).

helps.creator: none
helps.text:
Syntax: PK

If you are in a PK (player killing) church, you can be killed by
anyone who is also in a PK church.

In Neutral Player Killing rooms (npk), anybody can be killed
regardless of their level or whether they are in a church or not.

If you die in Chaotic Player Killing room (cpk), all of your
equipment remains in your corpse unless it has both the "nodrop"
and "nouncurse" flags. The equipment will remain in your corpse,
free for everyone to loot which makes CPK quite risky.

helps.creator: none
helps.text:
Syntax: pursuit
 
When activated, the pursuit skill will move you after fleeing players
and NPCs automatically. There is a chance for it to fail, depending on
your proficiency at it.

helps.creator: none
helps.text:
Quarterstaff is the ability to wield and use a 
quarterstaff in battle. Their knowledge in this
particular skill will determine how much damage
one does with this weapon.
 
see also: EXOTIC AXE DAGGER SPEAR SWORD FLAIL MACE
          POLEARM WHIP WEAPONS BOW and CROSSBOW

helps.creator: Syn
helps.text:
Syntax: shoot <target> [direction]
{x        throw <object> <target> [direction]
 
Ranged weapons are a way to get back at your foes without 
having to fight them in a melee battle.
 
Crossbows and bows are worn behind an archer's back and can be
worn at the same time as a melee weapon. The archer may also
wear a quiver on his or her shoulder to store bolts and arrows;
arrows loaded from a quiver greatly increase shooting speed.
 
The archery skill improves your accuracy and damage when shooting
bows and crossbows. If there are multiple targets around you
with the same name, you will be asked to specify a direction in which
to shoot.
 
Weapons may also be thrown in the same fashion. You do not have
to wield them first. They can only be throw with a range of one
room, however, unlike bows and arrows, which have a range.
of several rooms.

helps.creator: none
helps.text:
Syntax: rescue <target>

Rescue allows you to step into combat and tank for somebody
who is getting wailed on. You can only rescue members of your
own formation, and you cannot rescue mobiles.

helps.creator: none
helps.text:
Shield and weapon style is a warrior's ability to
effectively fight with the use of a sword and shield.
The more knowledged they are in this skill, the better
chance they have to deflect blows and strike their 
opponent in return.

helps.creator: none
helps.text:
Single weapon style is a fighter's skill that when in
combat, one will use many ways and means to land their
hits, often times exciting a nearby crowd, or make an
opponent extremely angry. It is the style in which you
use your weapon.

helps.creator: none
helps.text:
Syntax: skull <corpse>
 
Skull is a brutal skill in where a warrior with a strong 
stomach rips the skull out of a dead corpse, keeping it
for his or her own private collection. The skulls of their
fallen opponents can either be kept for bragging rights,
or be used by a magic user to temporarily see through 
their eyes, knowing their location to find them again.

helps.creator: none
helps.text:
Syntax: slit <target>
 
Slit throat is an ancient, brutal skill in which 
an assassin will sneak up on their unsuspecting 
victim, and slit their throat, killing them 
instantly. This skill is one of the assassin's 
most promising attacks while avoiding the rules
of engagement. 
 
Note: Slit throat can only be used if an assassin
      has blackjacked, or put their opponent to
      sleep first.

helps.creator: Syn
helps.text:
Syntax: smite <person>
 
This skill channels either holy or cursed energies to finish off a foe
whose is near his end. The victim's health must be below 1/4 of his
total health for smite to work, and the user's weapon must be either
blessed (if he/she is evil) or cursed (if he/she is good).
Followers of Neutrality can use either a blessed or a cursed weapon
to smite their foes.

helps.creator: Syn
helps.text:
Syntax: trample <person>
 
Using the trample skill, a Crusader can charge a victim and run them
down with their mount. Extreme pain and the inability to move results.

helps.creator: none
helps.text:
Syntax: trip <target>
 
This skill allows one to trip their opponent in combat. This
does not work against flying creatures, or players with
levitation. This is a preferred attack of rogues and thieves.

helps.creator: none
helps.text:
Two-handed weapon style is a well known skill of the
warrior. The more skilled a warrior is in this trait, 
the better chance one will have of damaging their 
opponent with a two-handed weapon, using their weapons
with great skill.

helps.creator: Syn
helps.text:
Syntax:
{x  warcry
{x
The war cry skill allows Destroyers to infuse both themselves
and their party members with the destructive energy they are
known for. War cry increases the success chance of all of your 
defenses and attacks by 1.5x. It also raises your strength.

helps.creator: Syn
helps.text:
In addition to your skill with your weapon of choice, your proficiency at
your fighting style helps determine your overall aptitude. Knowing
the style well yields more accurate blows as well as more damage dealt.
 
Some common styles known to all are practiced in the land of Sentience,
as well as some more exotic ones only recently developed.

{YCommon styles:{x
{x  Single weapon style                  {Y-{x combat with a single weapon
{x  Two-handed weapon style              {Y-{x combat with a two-handed weapon
{x  Shield and weapon style              {Y-{x combat with a shield and a weapon
 
{YExotic styles:{x
{x  Wilderness spear style               {Y-{x combat with a spear
{x  Sword and dagger style               {Y-{x combat with a sword and dagger combination
{x  Mount and weapon style               {Y-{x combat on horseback

helps.keyword: WEAPONS AXE DAGGER FLAIL MACE POLEARM SPEAR SWORD WHIP QUARTERSTAFF EXOTIC
helps.creator: none
helps.text:
Each weapon skill applies to a specific group of weapons,
and determines how well a character fights with a particular
weapon.

In Sentience, the following types of weapons are known:

{YAxe{x             : the use of axes
{YDagger{x          : the use of stabbing weapons
{YFlail{x           : the use of ball-and-chain type weapons
{YMace{x            : the use of blunt, bashing weapons such
{YPolearm{x         : the use of long-range slashing weapons
{YSpear{x           : the use of long-ranged stabbing weapons
{YSword{x           : the use of short-range slashing weapons
{YWhip{x            : the use of whips and chains
{YQuarterstaff{x    : the use of long wooden staves
{YExotic{x          : the use of strange or magical weapons

helps.creator: Syn
helps.text:
Syntax:
{x  weave <target>
 
Using this skill, a warlord can switch his/her focus to a different
enemy in battle by dextrously weaving in and out of combat. If the
skill is successful, he/she will begin attacking the target.

helps.creator: none
helps.text:
This fighting style is a favorite among Rangers while they are on deep
expeditions in the forest.  If wielding a spear (with or without a shield) a
ranger can anticipate attacks from other, ward them off, and strike very
quickly back with their spear.  They can also use the spear to block attacks
in combat, although this works less often than other defenses.  This skill
works whether the spear is wielded as a primary or secondary weapon.

helps.creator: none
helps.text:
Syntax: wimpy
		wimpy <hit points>

Wimpy lets you set a value which triggers an automatic flee
if your hp drops below it. With a wimpy of 90, you would automatically
attempt to flee as soon as your HP drops below 90. Wimpy
without an argument sets the value to 20% of your max hp.

helps.keyword: CHANNELS TELL SHOUT YELL GOSSIP OOC SAY
helps.creator: none
helps.text:
Syntax: <channel> <message>
 
Channels are your way to communicate with other
players on Sentience. They can be turned on and
off by each player by typing a channel name.
 
(If a channel is off, you do not hear it).
 
CHANNELS shows you all channels and their status.
 
GOSSIP, OOC, and FLAME are all global and are heard
by all players.
 
GOSSIP & OOC allow a tag to be attached to the front of your
message.  The tag can be up to 10 characters long and
may have up to 3 colors (Ending with magenta for your text).

YELL - is heard by all players in your area.
SAY  - is heard by all players in your room.
TELL - is heard by a single player anywhere
       in the game.

The HELPER channel can be used by just about anyone (especially
new players who have not had much experience with the game) to page
the available people with {W[H]{x (helper) status. Only helpers
and immortals can see this channel, so it's a great place to go
if you don't feel comfortable asking for help over another public
channel and want to talk to someone who is both knowledgeable
about the game and interested in helping other players.
 
The following channels are heard by ALL players who have them on:
ANNOUNCEMENTS - Crier announcements (show people leveling and multiclassing)
AUCTION - Shows auction messages (help auction)
GOSSIP - For game related gossip ONLY.
OOC    - Out of character (non game related stuff) 
FLAME {x - For flaming, bitching, whining, etc.

helps.creator: Syn
helps.text:
Chat is mostly for idling. You type /enter, then go afk.
However if you want to actually chat there are some features
for that.
 
Most of the commands are pretty self-explanatory (type "chat"
for a list). If you're too lazy to type "chat", "/" is an
abbrevation for it.

helps.creator: Syn
helps.text:
Syn knows how to check his email.  Please don't ask him if he's gotten
your email, because he has, or tell him that you've emailed him, because
he'll know when he gets it.  
 
The forbidden questions:
"Have you got my note?"
"Have you got my email?"
 
Those who ask the supreme being of the universe these questions are subject
to extreme crankiness, grumbling, and/or midget throwing.

helps.creator: none
helps.text:
Syntax: emote <action>

EMOTE shows an action to everybody in the room. 'emote runs 
around foolishly' would show 'Karnak runs around foolishly'
to everybody in the room, assuming you are Karnak.

helps.creator: none
helps.text:
Syntax ft <message>
 
FT sends a message to all of the members in a formation.
 
see also: GROUP

helps.creator: none
helps.text:
This is the skill of negotiating the price up for an item you are selling,
or down for an item you are buying. The amount you kick the price up or down
depends solely on your level and skill in haggling. In fact, certain people
are so good at haggling with their golden tongues that they buy items for
negative amounts. (take my merchandise and my money, please!)

helps.creator: Syn
helps.text:
Helpers are people picked by Immortals to assist the players of the game
with their needs.  They do not have any special powers aside from being able
to see the helper channel.  We try to pick the most knowledgeable and
friendly people for this job.  
 
They are obligated to answer your questions about game function (for example:
what does a skill do, what command lets you toggle so-and-so, what is this channel
for, what does this rule mean).
 
When it comes to specifics of what is located where as far as items or NPCs, it's 
really up to the helpers on duty. They will usually be glad to assist newer players
with such queries but are generally instructed to give hints (to quests, item locations,
etc., rather than telling you outright).
 
We'll add more to this helpfile shortly, but a little bit is better than nothing. 8)

helps.creator: none
helps.text:
Immortals are anyone of level 150 or above. They are bound by obligation
to help mortals, unless of course the mortals are being unruly, in which
case they're bound by obligation to maim or dismember them.

Any problems within the game which cannot be resolved between mortals
should be taken to any imm.

Also see: RULES, especially #6.

categories.name: ifchecks
categories.description: Contains help topics pertaining to if-checks used in scripting.
categories.creator: Syn

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if act $-code actions
Operates on: Mobiles
{x
Checks to see if the mobile has the given action flag.  This does not
check for act2 flags, however.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if affected $-code affects
Operates on: Mobiles
{x
Checks to see if the mobile has the affect bit set.  This only looks
at the FIRST bank of affect bits.  Affect2 is not checked by this,
and no such if-check exists yet to do this.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if align $-code comparison integer
Operates on: Mobiles
{x
Compares the alignment of the mobile against the integer.  Evil alignments
are negative.  Good alignments are positive.  Neutral alignment is zero.
The is-alignment if-checks deal with these in a more general sense in that
one does not need to know what numbers do what with the alignments.  However,
to check for sub-ranges in alignments, this if-check is needed.
{x
See also IF-CHECK ISEVIL, IF-CHECK ISGOOD, IF-CHECK ISNEUTRAL.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if carries $-code target
             if wears $-code target
Operates on: Mobiles
{x
Checks to see if the mobile carries or wears/wields/holds the given object
target, which can be specified as either a vnum or a name.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if church $-code name
Operates on: Players
{x
Checks to see if the player is a member of the specified church.  This
returns false if the church doesn't exist or the player is churchless.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if class $-code name
Operates on: Mobiles
{x
Checks to see if the mobile's current class is the specified name.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if clones comparison integer
Operates on: Mobiles
{x
Determines if the number of clones of the mobile enactor mobile
exist in the current room.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if deitypoint $-code comparison integer
Operates on: Players
{x
Compares the number of deity points the player has against the number.
Primarily used by Geldoff in the Maze along with the DECDEITY command
to deduct dp for life restore.
{x
See also MPROG COMMAND DECDEITY.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if exitexists direction
Operates on: Rooms
{x
Checks to see if the exit in the given direction exists.  Often used
with the LINK script command to create/delete temporary exits.  The
direction supplied is given in word form (north, east, down, etc).
{x
See also RPROG OPROG MPROG COMMAND LINK.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if grpsize $-code comparison integer
Operates on: Mobiles
{x
Compares the size of the target's group against the integer.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if has $-code type
             if uses $-code type
Operates on: Mobiles
{x
Checks to see if the mobile carries or uses (wears, wields or holds)
an object of the given type.
{x
See also OEDIT OBJECT TYPES.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if hasship $-code
Operates on: Players
{x
Checks to see if the target has a ship.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if hastarget $-code
Operates on: Mobiles, Objects, Rooms
{x
Checks to see if the target's script target ($q) is in the room with it.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if hour comparison integer
Operates on: Nothing
{x
Compares the in-game hour against the integer.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if hpcnt $-code comparison integer
Operates on: Mobiles
{x
Computes the hitpoint percentage of the mobile and compares it against
the integer.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if imm $-code immunity
Operates on: Mobiles
{x
Checks to see if the mobile has the immunity flags.  Currently, there
is no way to check for resistances or vulnerabilities.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if isactive $-code
Operates on: Mobiles
{x
Checks to see if the mobile is awake (position > SLEEPING).

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if isangel $-code
             if isdemon $-code
             if ismystic $-code
Operates on: Mobiles
{x
Checks to see if the mobile is either an angel, demon or mystic.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if ischarm $-code
Operates on: Mobiles
{x
Checks to see if the mobile is charmed.  This is equivalent to
testing the affected flag for charmed.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if isdead $-code
Operates on: Mobiles
{x
Checks to see if the mobile dead.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if isdelay $-code
Operates on: Mobiles, Objects, Rooms
{x
Checks to see if the enactor has a delay timer pending.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if isevil $-code
             if isgood $-code
             if isneutral $-code
Operates on: Mobiles
{x
Checks to see if the mobile's alignment fits with the particular
classification.  Grades of alignment are not checked.  A satanic
mobile will make isevil true, just as a malevolent mobile.
{x
See also IF-CHECK ALIGN.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if isfollow $-code
Operates on: Mobiles
{x
Checks to see if the mobile is both a follower and if so, if their
master is in the room.  Both have to be the case for this to be true.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if isimmort $-code
Operates on: Mobiles
{x
This determines if the mobile is an immortal, but rather crudely.
This merely checks to see if the level is at least 150, so mobiles
over this level will be treated as an immortal.  Use this in
conjunction with ISPC to check for TRUE immortals.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if isnpc $-code
             if ispc $-code
Operates on: Mobiles
{x
Checks to see if the target is an npc or a player, respectively.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if istarget $-code
Operates on: Mobiles
{x
Checks to see if the target the remembered target of the script.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if isvisible $-code
Operates on: Mobiles, Objects
{x
Checks to see if the target is visible to the script enactor.
Objects and rooms can see everything, so this only makes sense
in mobile scripts.  Blindness, invisibility and darkness will
affect whether the mobile can see the target.  Invisible mobiles
will show up as someone.  Invisible objects will show up as
something.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if level $-code comparison integer
{x
Compares the level of the mobile against the specified number.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if mobexists target
             if objexists target
Operates on: Nothing
{x
Checks to see if there is a mobile or object of the given target
loaded in the world.  One can check for Nth copy of a target by
using the number-dot notation (#.target).

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if mobhere target
             if objhere target
Operates on: Nothing
{x
Checks to see if there is a mobile or object of the given target
in the current room.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if mobs comparison integer
             if players comparison integer
             if people comparison integer
Operates on: Nothing
{x
Compares the number of npcs, players and mobiles in the current room
that can be seen by the script against the supplied integer.  PEOPLE
equals to the sum of MOBS and PLAYERS.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if money $-code comparison integer
Operates on: Mobiles
{x
Computes the total silver the mobile possesses, consisting of the gold
multiplied by one hundred added to the silvers, comparing the result
against the supplied number.  This works well in conjuction with the
script command CHARGE to create transactions.
{x
See also MPROG COMMAND CHARGE.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if name $-code string
Operates on: Mobiles, Objects
{x
Does a prefix name comparison of the specified string against the name
of the target.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if objtype $-code type
Operates on: Objects
{x
Checks to see if the object is the given type.

helps.keyword: IF-CHECK OBJVAL0 OBJVAL1 OBJVAL2 OBJVAL3 OBJVAL4
helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if objval# $-code comparison integer
Operates on: Objects
{x
Compares the specific object value (v# from oedit) against the
integer.  Note, values that are flags or types in oedit are NUMBERS
with these if-checks.  If checking against, say, a fountain, one
can check the liquid type by comparing value two against the index
in the liquid table for the particular liquid you wish to check
against, starting with 0(zero) for water.  Currently, only v0 to
v4 can be checked with the if-checks.  The rest of the values are
inaccessible at this point in time.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if off $-code offense
Operates on: Mobiles
{x
Used to see if the NPC mobile has the given offense flags set,
such as dodge or assist_vnum.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if order comparison integer
Operates on: Nothing
{x
Used to determine the order in which the enactor reacted to a trigger,
starting with order 1(one).

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if pos $-code position
Operates on: Mobiles
{x
Compares the position of the mobile against the specified position.
Valid positions are those that can be set on mobiles.  View {Y? pos{x in
the OLC editors.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if questpoint $-code comparison integer
Operates on: Players
{x
Compares the number of quest points the player has acquired against the
integer.
{x
Note: Will become obsolete or reworked due to changes in how quest points
      are stored.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if race $-code string
Operates on: Mobiles
{x
Checks to see if the mobile's race is the specified string.  The race must
be one of the defined races.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if rand integer
Operates on: Nothing
{x
Computes a random percentage and compares it against the number given.
The if-check is true if the supplied number is greater than the random
percentage.
{x
Note: This if-check used to have the opposite polarity due to a bug,
      so older scripts that have used this if-check may function
      differently.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if room $-code comparison integer
Operates on: Mobiles, Objects
{x
Compares the vnum of the room the target is in against the specified
number.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if sex $-code comparison integer
Operates on: Mobiles
{x
Checks against the mobile's sex.  The integer value must be one of three
values: 0 for Neuter, 1 for Male, 2 for Female.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax:      if vnum $-code comparison integer
Operates on: Mobiles, Objects
{x
Checks to see if the mobile or object's vnum compares to the integer.
Players have a vnum of 0(zero).

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
If-checks provide scripts with various decision making statements for
flow control, coming in five classes based upon their syntax structure. 
{x
See also IF-CHECKS SYNTAX, IF-CHECKS $-CODES, IF-CHECKS INDEX.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
{x               enactor actor target random saved primary secondary
-------------------------------------------------------------------
name          |  $i   |  $n |  $t  |  $r  |  $q |  $o   |  $p
short         |  $I   |  $N |  $T  |  $R  |  $Q |  $O   |  $P
he/she/it     |  $j   |  $e |  $E  |  $J  |     |       |
him/her/it    |  $k   |  $m |  $M  |  $K  |     |       |
his/her/its   |  $l   |  $s |  $S  |  $L  |     |       |
-------------------------------------------------------------------
{x
enactor         What executes the script
actor           What triggers the script
target          The target of the script
random          A random character in the room
saved           The saved mob of the enactor
primary         First object in the trigger
secondary       Second object in the trigger

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
{x
act             affected        align           carries         
church          class           clones          deitypoint      
exitexists      grpsize         has             hasship
hastarget       hour            hpcnt           imm

isdelay         isdemon         isevil          isfollow
isgood          isimmort        ismystic        isneutral
isnpc           ispc            istarget        isvisible
level           mobexists       mobhere         mobs
money           name            objexists       objhere
objtype         objval0         objval1         objval2
objval3         objval4         off             order
people          players         pos             questpoint
race            rand            room            sex

{x
To view an if-check helpfile, see IF-CHECK name.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
{x
If-check Syntax Classes
-------------------------------------------
1       if-check value
2       if-check comparison number
3       if-check $-code
4       if-check $-code value
5       if-check $-code comparison number
-------------------------------------------
{x
If-check Comparisons
-------------------------------------------
==      Equal
==      Equal
>       Greater-than
>=      Greater-than or Equal
<       Less-than
<=      Less-than or Equal
-------------------------------------------
{x

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: appear
        disappear
{x
The mobile will become wizinvis based upon its set level, which means it
can disappear for immortals (not sure about Imps) since a level 200 mobile
will have a wizinvis level of 200, which is higher than all immortals.
For simple wizimobs, one can just use the wizi_mob act2 flag.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: cast spell [target]
{x
Performs an IMMEDIATE spell cast for the specified spell, using no mana.
The target is optional.  No "begins casting" message is given, just the
resultant spell function.  The level of the spell is set to the level of
the object or mobile performing the spell.  Be warned, though, some spells
look very strange when objects cast them.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: asound message
{x
Echoes the message to adjacent rooms.
{x
See also RPROG OPROG MPROG COMMAND ECHO.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: at location command
{x
Performs a command remotely at the given location.  Useful to do slight of
hand tricks or to conceal various messages that would otherwise reveal
what the mobile is doing.  When rooms use the AT command, they can only
do room commands, as that is all they can ever do period, given without
the room prefix.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: call vnum victim param1 param2
{x
Calls a subroutine script at the vnum.  The victim becomes the actor
in the script.  All but the vnum can be left as NULL (or omitted).

helps.keyword: RPROG OPROG MPROG COMMAND CANCEL DELAY
helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: delay duration
        cancel
{x
Sets the delay timer on the room, object or mobile.  The timer will
not decrement if there is no defined DELAY trigger.  The duration is
measured in pulses for mobiles and ticks for rooms and objects.
{x
Cancel will clear the delay timer, if active.
{x
See also RPROG OPROG MPROG TRIGGER DELAY and
         TICKS AND PULSES.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: damage victim min max [lethal]
{x
Does unconditional damage to the victim, ranging from the minimum
to maximum damage.  Lethal damage bypasses safeguards such as armor
class, spells, etc... and can KILL (hence the term lethal).  Without
lethal set, the victim's hit points does not go below 1.

helps.keyword: RPROG OPROG MPROG COMMAND ECHO ECHOAT ECHOAROUND GECHO ZECHO
helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: echo message
        echoat target message
        echoaround target message
        gecho message
        zecho message
{x
Echoes message to everyone in the room, at the target, to everyone
in the room but the target, every online player and every online
player in the same zone, respectively.

helps.keyword: RPROG OPROG MPROG COMMAND FORCE GFORCE VFORCE
helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: force target command
        gforce target command
{x
Attempts to force the target to do a command.  When mobiles do it,
the mobile must be ABLE to force the target.  Rooms and objects
can force any player.  Immortals, however, cannot be forced, for
obvious security reasons.
{x
Gforce will attempt to force the target's group, with the same
restrictions as force.  Vforce is different in that it will force
the first loaded mobile of the supplied vnum to do the command.

helps.keyword: RPROG OPROG MPROG COMMAND FORGET REMEMBER
helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: remember target
        forget
{x
Used to remember a MOBILE target which can be referenced by the
Saved $-code ($q).  Forget will reset the code.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: link direction vnum/delete
{x
Either creates an open, doorless exit in the direction to the specified vnum
or deletes the exit.  Created exits are not saved in asave.  This is great
for creating scripted/temporary exits.

helps.keyword: RPROG OPROG MPROG COMMAND MLOAD OLOAD
helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: mload vnum
        oload vnum [level [room|inside]]
{x
Loads either a mobile or an object specified by the vnum.  For objects, the
level sets the level of the object.
{x
When done by a mobile, supplying the parameter room loads the object into
the room, otherwise, it loads in the mobile's inventory.
{x
When done by an object, supplying the parameter inside loads the object
inside, usually with containers.  Otherwise, it loads into the room.

helps.keyword: RPROG OPROG MPROG COMMAND PURGE SELFDESTRUCT
helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: purge target
        selfdestruct
{x
Purge will destroy the mobile or object target from the current room,
provided it can be purged.  A very dangerous scenario involves the
use of purge $i in mobile or object script, which will destroy the
enactor.  Very bad if there are more statements, and can suffer the
horrible plague of targeting the WRONG target.  Rooms cannot be purged,
so don't bother trying.
{x
In light of the purge $i problems, there are times when that is what
is desired, the enactor purging itself.  Due to the fallable targeting
methods, the command selfdestruct was created.  That WILL target the
enactor and ONLY the enactor.  Rooms cannot selfdestruct, though.
{x
With either command, if the enactor is purged/selfdestructed, it had
better be the LAST command the script executes before the end of script
or a break statement.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: remove target vnum|all
{x
A powerful command in that it can remove EVERYTHING from the target's
inventory, including the shirt off their back.  If a vnum is supplied,
all instances of that vnum worn or in the main inventory are removed.
Matching items contained in containers ignored.  Using all will simply
do everything in their inventory, worn or not, which is why this command
is so dangerous if handled improperly.

helps.keyword: RPROG OPROG MPROG COMMAND TRANSFER GTRANSFER GOTO
helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: transfer target [location]
        gtransfer target [location]
        otransfer object [location]
        goto location
{x
Transfers the target to the specified location.  If the location is omitted,
the target is transfered to the current room.  The target will do a look upon
transfer.  Gtransfer will transfer the target's entire group.  Otransfer works
on objects.
{x
Goto is a silent teleport used by mobiles and objects to move to a different
location.

helps.keyword: MPROG COMMAND AIRSHIPADDWAYPOINT AIRSHIPSETCRASH CHANGEVESSELNAME RESTRICTED
helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: airshipaddwaypoint
        airshipsetcrash
        changevesselname
{x
Not sure what these do exactly, so DO NOT TRY TO USE THEM!  They are
most assuredly involved with the airship and ships (no kidding).

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: assist target
{x
Causes the mobile to assist the target in combat, simulating the assist
offense flags, but with scriptable control.
{x
See also MEDIT OFFENSES

helps.keyword: MPROG COMMAND AWARDGOLD AWAREPNEUMA AWARDPRAC AWARDQP AWARDXP RESTRICTED
helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: awardgold target amount
        awardpneuma target amount
        awardprac target amount
        awardqp target amount
        awardxp target amount
{x
Gives the target the specified amount of gold, pneuma, practices,
quest points and experience respectively.  These commands are LOGGED,
so get permission from an Imp to use them.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: charge target min max
{x
Deducts the random amount of money in the given range from the target's
wealth.  It does not check to see if the target has sufficient wealth
to do so.  Use the MONEY if-check for this purpose.  Used in conjunction,
one can create scriptable purchases that perform true money transactions.
{x
See also IF-CHECK MONEY.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: decdeity target amount
{x
Command used by Geldoff to deduct the specified deity points from
the target.  Although, this can obviously be used by other mobiles
for purposes other than resurrection, but get Imp permission to use
this.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: flee
{x
Makes the mobile attempt to flee, simulating the wimpy action.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: junk object|all
{x
Junks all objects in the mobile's main inventory that match the pattern
or vnum.  If all is used, the entire inventory is junked.  This is the
same as doing remove $i object|all.
{x
See also MPROG COMMAND REMOVE.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: kill target
{x
Attempts to initiate combat with the target.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: raisedead target
{x
Primarily performed by Geldoff to raise the target from the dead,
as long as the target IS dead.  This highly powerful command likely
CAN be used elsewhere for the same purposes, but this requires Imp
permission to do so.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: teleport
{x
This functions akin to the old teleport spell, only silently, teleporting
the mobile to a random room.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: zot victim
{x
Does a glorious zot.  (As if there's any other kind!)  Get permission from
an Imp to use this command, as it's not nice to zot people for no reason.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: addmprog vnum board %
{x
When someone boards a ship the mobile is on, their Board triggers will
be checked.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: addmprog vnum bribe silver
{x
A rather archaic trigger, Bribes are used when you give the
mobile a given amount of money measured in silver.  The problems
with this trigger are many.  First, if you give too much, there
is no way the scripts involved can know that.  Second, it has
no idea how you gave it.  Silver? Gold? How?  It can't do things
like return money, as the script has no idea how it was given.
Third, if you give too little money to activate any bribe
trigger, giving more will not "add" to it.  This trigger is
just cumbersome to handle exchange of money, especially if the
impetus that drove the actions was, say, a speech trigger or
a give trigger.
{x
There are other ways to do this.  There is a script command
that can charge a target a given range of money (measured in
silver).
{x
See also MPROG COMMAND CHARGE.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: addmprog vnum death %
{x
It is often desired for a mobile to do something when it dies.
This trigger will do that, be it to load some objects or simply
to echo special messages.  Certain caveats have to be taken into
account when dealing with this trigger.  One, the standard death
cry messages will show up, regardless if the mob does a death
script or not.  Two, if dropping items, blinded mobs will be
unable to do so.  Three, projectiles caught in the inventory of
the mob should be dropped if the mob does not remain in the room.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: addmprog vnum entry %
{x
When a mobile wanders around, it checks for entry triggers that
are used in each room the mobile enters.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: addmprog vnum exit direction
{x
The difference between this trigger and the ExAll is visibility.
If the mobile cannot see you, this will not fire.
{x
See also MPROG TRIGGER EXALL.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: addmprog vnum flee %
{x
Flee triggers are checked when opponents attempt to flee from a fight,
allowing mobiles to react.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: addmprog vnum give target
{x
Give triggers are nifty tools, especially for quests.  One can
set the trigger to filter for a specific object vnum or use
a name string to allow groups of objects that match the string.
Or, you can just use the word all to indicate that it will fire
for any object given to it.  The only exception is if money is
given.  That will check for Bribe triggers.
{x
See also MPROG TRIGGER BRIBE.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: addmprog vnum greet %
{x
Greet triggers, as opposed to GrAll triggers, only fire when
a target enters the room that the mobile can see.
{x
See also MPROG TRIGGER GRALL.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: addmprog vnum hpcnt %hp
{x
When the mob's hitpoint percentage drops to the specified value,
this trigger will fire, often used for simulated wimpy.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: addmprog vnum kill %
{x
When someone attacks the mobile, this trigger will fire.  This
has various uses, such as a guard calling for reinforcements
or wielding weaponry.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: addmprog vnum prereckoning %
        addmprog vnum reckoning %
{x
These triggers function as Random triggers during the signs
of the Reckoning and the Reckoning itself, respectively.
{x
See also MPROG TRIGGER RANDOM.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: addmprog vnum repop %
{x
When an area repops a mobile, this trigger is checked, useful
for loading equipment randomly.
{x

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: addmprog vnum whisper string
{x
Similar to the Speech trigger, Whisper triggers react to speech.
However, they only react to... yes, whispers.  When someone
whispers to the mobile, whisper triggers are checked.
{x
See also MPROG TRIGGER SPEECH.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Mobile triggers handle an expanded set compared to the room triggers, as
well as various interactions with the mobile, such as death and
communication.  Unlike room and object triggers, mobiles have to deal with
visibility issues.  Some triggers will NOT fire if the mobile cannot see the
target.  Others fire regardless.  If a target is invisible to the mobile,
its $-codes will show up as someone or something.  It is best to code around
such things. 
{x
Current list of oprog triggers: (See also {Y? mprog{x in any editor)
act             board           bribe           death
delay           entry           exall           exit
fight           flee            give            grall
greet           hpcnt           kill            prereckoning
random          reckoning       repop           speech
whisper
{x
View help for a particular trigger with {Yhelp MPROG TRIGGER {Wtype{x.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: addoprog vnum fight %
addmprog vnum fight %
{x
Checked each fight pulse, this trigger is used to give the object
or mobile special combat actions.  The object in question refers
to wielded weapons only.  The $n in the scripts refers to the
opponent.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: addoprog vnum drink %
        addoprog vnum eat %
{x
Drink triggers are checked when drink containers and fountains
are drank from.  Since drink containers can be refilled, it is
best to check the liquid type by comparing the liquid number
against the liquid table.  The first liquid has a number of 0.
{x
When foods or pills are eaten, they can fire Eat scripts.
Do NOT destruct the object in these scripts as it's already
handled by the system.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: addoprog vnum drop %
{x
The Drop trigger can be used on anything takable as well as
cart objects.  Ok, it can be placed on any other object, but
it doesn't make sense to be used on things that cannot be
dropped.  The very act of dropping is done first, which allows
Drop scripts to do destructive things to itself, that is,
self-destruct.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: addoprog vnum get %
{x
Picking up takable objects will test their Get triggers,
useful for having things happen should the wrong individual
tries to grab it.  However, the act of getting the item has
already been done, so if you wish they did NOT have the item,
they have to be forced to drop it or some other command.
{x
Note: This does not work when getting objects from a container.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: addoprog vnum pull %
        addoprog vnum push %
        addoprog vnum turn %
{x
Manipulating an object is rather difficult for the most part,
as there is no way to articulate every possible action without
going overboard.  Three basic actions aside from Get and Drop
can be done: Pull, Push and Turn.  As their names imply, they
involve simple movements on the object.
{x
One caveat with Pull: pulling a cart with a Pull trigger will
test for the trigger, not do the normal action with the cart.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: addoprog vnum throw %
{x
Thrown objects will check for Throw triggers.  The current room of
the script(s) is the room of the throw target.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: addoprog vnum wear %
{x
When using armor, weapons or anything else wearable/holdable,
this trigger is checked.  Many examples have the object echo
special messages unique to the item.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Object triggers handle a small set of interactions with objects, though
there could be more.  Many deal with actions done to the objects.  One needs
to take note that these actions are completed BEFORE the triggers are
called, so scripts have to be coded accordingly. 
{x
Current list of oprog triggers: (See also {Y? oprog{x in any editor)
act             delay           drink           drop
eat             exall           fight           get
grall           pull            push            random
speech          throw           turn            wear
{x
View help for a particular trigger with {Yhelp OPROG TRIGGER {Wtype{x.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: addrprog vnum act string
        addoprog vnum act string
        addmprog vnum act string
{x
Act triggers are used to match to the input of the internal act() function.
Be warned, the string used to match on is sometimes difficult to do.  It can
be a simple phrase seen in messages to the full message in the raw form. What
is meant by raw form is that the string contains various $-codes used to
represent you, mobs, targets, objects, doors, etc.  Basically, any message
that other people can see, act triggers can check on.  These will not trap on
script echoes.  There are definite problems with the trigger, though if used
correctly can work well.
{x
Example 1:
     addrprog 1234 act "$p flows from the ground."
{x
     This example adds an act trigger to the room that checks for the message
     done when "create spring" has been cast.
{x
Example 2:
     addmprog 1234 act "$n begins casting a spell..."
{x
     This example shows how to make a mob trigger on spell casting.
{x

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: addrprog vnum delay %
        addoprog vnum delay %
        addmprog vnum delay %
{x
Delay triggers are used for, well, delayed responses.  They are
checked if the delay timer expires, which can be set within scripts
using the delay command.  Two things to note about these triggers.
First, there is only one delay timer per room/mobile/object, thus
can only have one delay going at a time.  Second, if there is NO
delay trigger defined on the index, the timer will NOT decrement.
When the timer expires, all defined delay triggers are checked in
series.  In the future, there is hope that one can have multiple
timers or be able to select which script to call.
{x
See also TICKS AND PULSES.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: addrprog vnum exall direction
        addoprog vnum exall direction
        addmprog vnum exall direction
{x
ExAll (Exit All) triggers fire when a target attempts to move in the
specified direction, regardless if there IS an exit there or not.
Visibility is not an issue with this trigger.  They fire whether the
target can be seen or not.
{x
See also MPROG TRIGGER EXIT.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: addrprog vnum grall %
        addoprog vnum grall %
        addmprog vnum grall %
{x
GrAll (Greet All) triggers fire when a target enters the room,
regardless if the subject can see the target.
{x
See also MPROG TRIGGER GREET.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: addrprog vnum random %
        addoprog vnum random %
        addmprog vnum random %
{x
Random triggers give a supposed "realism" to the game by having
various actions occur randomly, checked at the entity's particular
clock interval.
{x
See also TICKS AND PULSES.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Syntax: addrprog vnum speech string
        addoprog vnum speech string
        addmprog vnum speech string
{x
Speech triggers are used to check for various speech done.  For rooms and
objects, these are limited to things down via say.  Mobiles, however, can
react to tells using speech triggers.  These triggers are very difficult
to control if the trigger phrase is too short and/or too common.  For this
reason, one way to handle speech triggers is to use multi-word phrases or
even whole sentences.  The less likely someone will say the entire phrase
without doing the trigger inadvertantly the better it will look.
{x
Example 1:
     addrprog 1234 speech !
{x
     This example is a rather bizarre trigger.  What this does is trigger
     on exclamations, ie "shouting."  One use for this is to cause cave-ins
     if people got too loud.
{x
Example 2:
     addmprog 1234 speech "let me in"
{x
     This has a mob listen for someone saying "let me in" in their speech.
     This could do anything from checking for permission with transfers to
     fighting.  Who knows.
{x
See also MPROG TRIGGER WHISPER.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
The set of room triggers is rather sparse right now, dealing with
movement, actions and speech for the most part.
{x
Current list of rprog triggers: (See also {Y? rprog{x in any editor)
act             delay           exall           grall
random          speech
{x
To view help for a particular trigger, type {Yhelp RPROG TRIGGER {Wtype{x.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
To aide with deciphering the various triggers, this legend will explain
what the different parameters stand for.
{x
%           A number from 0 to 100 (a percentage chance)
%hp         A number from 0 to 100 (percent hitpoints)
direction   A number from 0 to 9, representing the exit number.
                  0 = north      1 = east       2 = south
                  3 = west       4 = up         5 = down
                  6 = northeast  7 = northwest  8 = southeast
                  9 = southwest
silver      A number representing silver, though can be combination
                  of gold and silver.  Formula: 100*gold + silver
string      A string to match on.  To do more than one word, use quotes
target      A name, vnum or "all"

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Triggers are ways for entities in the game to interact with events in the
environment.  Each type of entity has a seperate set of triggers, used to
take advantage of various aspects.  Currently, there are triggers for rooms,
objects and mobiles.  For convenience, a seperate help category has been
allocated for each set.  Please review the help files RPROG TRIGGERS, OPROG

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Scripts serve no purpose without commands.  Ordinary game commands may be
given, but without specialized commands, scripts are rather limited.  As
part of the scripting system, each type of script has a set of commands they
can execute, explained in the helpfiles to some degree.  Currently, there
are only three types of scripts: room, obj and mob scripts.  To execute a
command within a script of a particular type, enter a command in the
following form: {Ytype{W command{x, where the type is either room, obj or
mob. 
{x
Here are examples of doing commands in each type of script:
The command is the ECHO command, common to all types.
{x
mob scripts:      {Ymob echo {Wmessage{x
room scripts:     {Yroom echo {Wmessage{x
object scripts:   {Yobj echo {Wmessage{x
{x
See RPROG OPROG MPROG COMMAND for a list of all command help
files.  The help files for any given command leave off the
room/obj/mob prefix, showing the command syntax itself. Remember
to put the appropriate prefix before the commands when using them
in scripts.  For instance, the help for ECHO shows {Yecho {Wmessage{x,
but to use it in, say, a room script, you would put {Yroom{x in
front of the command, ie. {Yroom echo {Wmessage{x.  Not all commands
are defined for each script type.  Be sure to check that the
particular *PROG keyword for the script type you wish to use is
listed for a given command.  RPROG is for rooms.  OPROG is for
objects.  And MPROG is for mobiles.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
There are currently two syntax constructs built into the scripting
system: break and the if statement.
{x
Syntax: break
{x
    Terminates the script execution.
{x
Syntax: if if-check
        [or if-check]
        ...
        [and if-check]
          [statements]
        [else
          [statements]]
        endif
{x
    The if statement is the only flow control method (a way to cause the
    program to choose a different route) available.  The break down is as
    follows:  You have the word IF followed by any of the defined if-checks
    using their respective syntax, followed by zero or more lines with OR or
    AND followed by a defined if-check, followed by zero or more valid script
    statements.  There then can be the word ELSE on a line by itself followed
    by zero or more valid script statements.  Finally, the entire if-statement
    is terminated by an ENDIF on a line by itself.
{x
    Valid script statements can be any valid command, a BREAK or another
    if statement (known as a nested if).
{x
See also IF-CHECKS.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
There are two timed events in the game: ticks and pulses.  The tick is
the minute interval that dominates just about everything in the game, from
spell durations to area repops.  A pulse, on the other hand, has a finer
granularity, having a few seconds between each pulse.  You find this in
combat.  But you also find it in mobile triggers.  The DELAY and RANDOM
triggers on mobiles run off the pulse clock instead of the tick clock as on
rooms and objects.  For delays, the timer duration is in pulses.  Random
triggers are checked every pulse.  So be careful in planning out triggers
for things, especially if there is timing involved.

helps.text:
{b                   ---{B----{C--- {YHELP EDITOR {C---{B----{b---{x
{x
Syntax:
{x  hedit
{x
{YOVERVIEW{x
HEDIT is the Sentience online help-editor system. It lets us add new helpfiles
and modify current ones without having to shut the game down.
{x
The interface is pretty simple. There are two things in it: help categories
and helpfiles. The categories are for organizational purposes - to help us 
make sense of the tons of documentation that make up the game. The helpfiles
are what actually store the meat of the help message.
{x
Categories are nested, one inside the other inside the other, as necesarry.
They are organized in a really really simplified directory structure, somewhat
like what Linux uses. The top-level category is the "root" category and holds 
all of the other main categories. When you type "hedit", it puts you in the
main category; from there you can browse the others using the HEDIT commands.
{x
Each category and each helpfile has a list of builders as well as a security
setting so we can assign different builders to work on different areas of
help without all hell breaking loose. The permissions are not recursive - 
that is, just because you have access to a category doesn't mean you will have
access to all of its sub-categories.
{x
It's highly suggested you set your prompt to have "%O" somewhere in your
prompt to keep track of where you are in the category structure and what
helpfile you are editing. This is a little bit different from the other 
editors in that if you're working on a help file, you will need to type "done"
to close that helpfile, then "done" again to close the editor. It's not by
any means hard to understand, but having %O in your prompt will help you.
 
{YHELP CATEGORIES{x
If you are in HEDIT but not editing a helpfile, hitting enter will show you
information about the category you are in. Here's a rundown of what the 
fields mean (most of them are self-explanatory):
{x
Name             - the category's name
Security         - minimum security to access or modify this category
Builders         - specific people with access to work in this category
Created by       - person who made this category
Created on       - time this category was made
Last modified by - last person who modified this category
Last modified on - time this category was last modified
Minimum level    - minimum level to VIEW helpfiles in this category
Description      - brief description of the category's contents
{x
In order to make helpfiles or other categories in a category, modify it 
in any way, or edit the helpfiles within it, you must have either as much
security as is specified by Security or be assigned as a builder. Usually,
we will assign people a category to work in and a list of helpfiles to do,
and you will go from there.
{x
Categories can be modified using the commands which will be listed below.
{x
{YHELPFILES{x
Helpfiles hold the actual text of the help database. This text is in a
helpfile. The edit command (while in HEDIT mode) will put you in the helpfile
editor. If you hit enter you will see information about the helpfile:
{x
Keywords         - the keywords used to pull up this helpfile using "help"
Security         - minimum security to access or modify this helpfile
Builders         - specific people with access to this helpfile
Created by       - person who made this helpfile
Created on       - time this helpfile was made
Last modified by - last person who modified this helpfile
Last modified on - time this helpfile was last modified
Category         - category this helpfile belongs to
Minimum level    - minimum level to VIEW this helpfile using "help"
{x
Each helpfile also has an arbitrary, unique index to allow access of help 
files with similar keywords and allow people to look up groups of related
helpfiles which share a keyword. These are assigned at reboot, not manually,
and they change all the time.

helps.creator: Tieryo
helps.text:
Object Editing: Points
 
Objects have a 'point' system to keep from getting too off balance. Without an IMP 'signing' an object, you will be limited in the beneficial affects it can be granted.
By default, objects will have a point value assigned based on their level, with a value of level/10 (so a level 100 object gets 10 points for bonuses).

When adding affects (via addaffect) or immune/res/vuln modifiers (via addimmune) these points are taken into account to determine if the change is allowed. Typically, negative modifiers will add to available points, while beneficial modifiers will deduct them. Note that the percentage change for a modifier to be applied factors into cost.
 
Immune/Res/Vuln costs:
Immunity: 5*chance/2
Resist: chance
Vuln: chance (bonus to points)
 
All three will then be further modifier as (modifier+9)/10.
Examples:
addimmune immune fire 10 (10% chance of item spawning with an 'immunity to fire' affect)
- This would deduct 3 points (5*10/2, then (25+9)/10) from the object's point pool.
addimmune vuln lightning 100 (100% chance of spawning with 'vulnerability to lightning' affect)
- This would add 10 points (100, then (100+9/10) to the object's point pool.
 
Affects:
HP or Mana: modifier/10
Movement: modifier/20
Dex/Wis/Int/Str/Con: modifier
AC: modifier/10
HR/DR: modifier/2
 
If an affect is negative, it is further modified by the random chance of application.
For negative affects under 10% chance of appearing, point bonus is reduced to 0.
For negative affects under 25% chance of appearing, point bonus is reduced by 75%
For negative affects under 50% chance of appearing, point bonus is reduced by 50%
For negative affects under 80% chance of appearing, point bonus is reduced by 20%
 
Finally, the cost is set to its absolute value, and applied. Negative affects will grant points, beneficial affects will remove them.
Example:
For a level 150-159 object, we have 15 points.
addaffect hp -100 10 (10% chance of -100 hp)
- This would add 2 points (-100/10 == -10, then -10/4 == -2.5) to the object's point pool
addaffect ac -100 10 (10% chance of adding -100 ac)
- This would deduct 10 points (-100/10 == -10) from the object's point pool.

The most common type of business is a shop, called a primary business,
as most areas have shops and several of them.  There are several kinds
of shops one can create, some requiring permission to install.  View
the help file for OLC SHOPS.
{x
Secondary businesses offer services instead of tangible objects persay.
There is a variety of types one can create: banks, post offices, locker
storage, healers and equipment repair.  Most require simple flags set
on either the room in question or the mobile providing the service.
Banks, post offices and lockers use room flags to designate their 
functionality.  The other two types reside on mobiles with the appropriate
action flag set.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Airship Ticket Sellers
{x
This shop type sells tickets for passage aboard the Goblin Airship.
Currently, there is only one location this exists, that being in Plith.
To be complete though, this is accomplished by setting the mobile
action flag airship_seller on whichever mobile you wish to sell tickets.
Given the nature of how the Goblin Airship functions, do not bother
asking for permission to use this.  There is very little chance of
multiple seller mobiles to be created.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
General and Pet Shops
{x
Two similar shops in structure, both shall be discussed here.  Both types
utilize room resets for stock inventories as well as needing a shopkeeper
to handle the shop commands.
{x
General shops use object resets in the room where the shopkeeper has its
reset.  Only objects loaded into the shopkeeper that have any value on
them are viable stock items.  Objects can also be loaded by scripts, but
their supply is limited to the number of objects loaded.  Objects loaded
by the reset list have an infinite supply.
{x
[ ][ ] 7407 - 10080> 
Example reset list:
Resets: M = mobile, R = room, O = object, P = pet, S = shopkeeper
 No.  Loads    Description       Location         Vnum   Mx Mn Description
==== ======== ============= =================== ======== ===== ===========
[ 1] M[ 7407] a sexy barten in room             R[ 7407]  1- 1 The Bar        
[ 2] O[ 7452] a bottle of f in the inventory of S[ 7407]       a sexy bartende
[ 3] O[ 7313] a shot glass  in the inventory of S[ 7407]       a sexy bartende
[ 4] O[ 7407] a wooden tabl in room             R[ 7407]       The Bar        
[ 5] O[ 7411] a bar stool   in room             R[ 7407]       The Bar       
{x
Shop list for example:
[ Lv    Price  Qty ] Item
[  1      150  --- ] a shot glass
[  1      450  --- ] a bottle of freshly brewed beer
{x
Notice the objects in the list are AFTER the shopkeeper mobile.  Notice
that the objects that do not show up but are in the shopkeeper's main
inventory have no value on them.
{x
Pet shops use mobiles instead of objects for stock.  These require some
planning as far as vnum usage.  All pet shops REQUIRE there be a room
immediately following the shopkeeper's reset room.  This means that if
the shopkeeper resets in room 1000, you will need to create a room at
vnum 1001.  This room is the storage room for all the mobiles.  Each
reset for the stock mobiles must be placed into this room.
{x
Both shop types require a shopkeeper mobile to be defined.  See the
help on shopkeepers at OLC SHOPKEEPERS.

helps.keyword: OLC SHOP SETUP SHIP CREW SELLER
helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Shipyards and Crew Sellers
{x
Shipyards are different than all other shops in that the only deciding
factor that creates a shipyard is the room flag ship_shop.  Once set,
the list command will show a list of available ships, regardless if
there is a mobile defined as a "shopkeeper".  In fact, this shop does
not need a shopkeeper to function.  This type of shop requires care
in placement as the area the shop is located affects where the ship
is loaded and what ships a player can buy.  Only create this after
consulting with an IMP for permission.
{x
Crew sellers provide crew mobiles for bought ships, offering a
predefined list of available choices.  This shop only requires
a mobile with the crew_seller action flag set.  As with shipyards,
get IMP permission before setting this on any mobile.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Trading Posts
{x
The commodities market is handled through trading posts, where the
only things sold are trade_type objects.  There is a predefined list
of trade types, each having their own pricing.  For a trading post
to be created, there needs to be a trader mobile built.  Set the
trader action flag on the appropriate mob and add a reset for its
location, and presto.  To use a trading post, buyers and sellers
must use a cart object in which the trade_type object are placed.
{x
Currently, the trading system is somewhat primitive in that the
trader mobiles do not keep track of the specific objects traded,
but only the types.  So special trade_type objects are not kept.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Shopkeepers
{x
Shopkeepers are special mobiles with shop data assigned to them
while in the mobile editor.  Shopkeeper data must be assigned for
certain type shops to function as the game code looks for mobiles
that have this data when people perform shop commands (list, buy,
etc).
{x
Syntax: shop command
{x
Commands:
hours open close      - sets the operation times of the shopkeeper.
                             the open hour must be less than the close
                             hour.  there is no way to have things like
                             an all-night tavern that is closed during
                             the day without some scripting to remove
                             the shopkeeper mobs when the shop is closed.
profit buy sell       - sets the markup (when buying) and markdown
                             (when selling) of items measured in
                             percentages.  100 represents normal
                             value.  50 represents half price.
                             200 represents double the price.
type number type      - sets the type of object the shopkeeper
                             will accept in a sell.  Once assigned,
                             the type cannot be removed, so plan
                             ahead.  Only five types can be set,
                             ranging from 0 to 4.
assign                - sets up the mob as a shopkeeper
remove                - removes the shopkeeper data
{x
See also OLC SHOPS.

helps.creator: Nibelung
helps.text:
Shops
{x
Shops are locations in the game that sell something, be it ordinary
objects or pets, even ships.  Everything requires money to purchase
items.  Not only is each type different in what they sell, setting
up each one requires a different set of commands.  The first two
shop types are generally open for any builder to make and the most
common in the game.  The remaining types are restricted and require
IMP permission to create.
{x
Be warned with shops.  Should there be two distinct shops/shopkeepers
in the room, only one will be accessible.
{x
There are six types of shops in the game:
general         - objects
pet             - pet mobs
ship            - ships
crew seller     - crew for ships
airship ticket  - trips aboard the airship
trading post    - trade items
{x
View setup help for a given type with OLC SHOP SETUP type.
{x
See also OLC SHOPKEEPERS.

helps.creator: Syn
helps.text:
Syntax:
{x  alist [placetype]
{x
Alist shows you a list of all the areas as well as
their names, vnum ranges, filename, security, 
and a list of builders assigned to the area. If the
area name is green, it is open to mortals, and if it
is red, it is closed to mortals.
{x
You can restrict the search by specifying a placetype;
acceptable placetypes are: first continent, second
continent, island, or other plane.

helps.creator: Syn
helps.text:
Syntax:
{x  asearch <keyword>
{x
Does a keyword search through the area list for one keyword.
For example, "asearch dungeon" would show you all of the areas
which have "Dungeon" in their name.

helps.creator: Syn
helps.text:
Syntax:
{x  mcopy <old vnum> <new vnum>
{x
Copies a mobile. It can be copied across areas
assuming you have security priveleges in both areas.

helps.creator: Syn
helps.text:
Syntax:
{x  mpcopy <old vnum> <new vnum>
{x
Copies a mob prog. It can be copied across areas
assuming you have security priveleges in both areas.

helps.creator: Syn
helps.text:
Syntax:
{x  ocopy <old vnum> <new vnum>
{x
Copies an object. It can be copied across areas
assuming you have security priveleges in both areas.
The imp-sig field isn't copied.

Extra Descriptions
{x

        ed delete keyword
